$comment: Canned replies for the stand-in platform (demo/fake-platform.js in the case desk engine), so this desk can be tried with no platform. Each key is a distinctive part of a case title, matched without regard to case. The stand-in adds its own first line saying that the reply is canned. The suppliers and their answers are invented. Start the stand-in with DESK_CONFIG pointing at desk.config.json in this folder.

replies.Larkspur:
Summary
Larkspur Cloud Archive Ltd hosts the bank's document archive, which holds customer information.
Tier 1, as the case states.
Clause 1.3 of MTB-STD-041 decides the requirements that apply: every requirement applies to a tier 1 supplier.
Case date: 16 November 2026. The assessment uses only the questionnaire and the passages of the standard handed over.

Draft assessment. For review by the third-party risk officer. Not issued.

| # | Requirement | Standard | Supplier's answer | Evidence relied on | Mark | Reason and what the officer should check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The supplier holds an independent security certification or audit report dated within the last 12 months. | MTB-STD-041 2.1 | Holds an independent security audit report | Independent security audit report, extract: "Report date: 15 September 2025." | not met | Supplier: report dated 15 September 2025; case date 16 November 2026; age 14 months. Limit: at most 12 months. 14 is more than 12, so the limit is missed. A missed limit is not met. Check whether a report dated within the last 12 months exists. |
| 2 | Customer information is encrypted at rest and in transit. | MTB-STD-041 2.2 | Encrypted at rest and in transit | Security overview, extract: "Customer information is encrypted at rest and in transit on every system that holds it." | met | The answer and the evidence both show what the requirement asks. |
| 3 | Multi-factor authentication is required for every member of the supplier's staff who can reach the bank's information, not only for administrators and not only for remote access. | MTB-STD-041 2.3 | Multi-factor sign-in for administrators | Access policy, extract: "Multi-factor authentication is required for administrator accounts. Other staff sign in with a password." | partly met | The supplier's own answer and the evidence agree that the control covers administrators only; the other staff who can reach the bank's information are not covered. Coverage of some of the staff but not all is partly met. Check which other staff can reach the bank's information. |
| 4 | The supplier tells the bank of a security incident that affects the bank within 24 hours of detecting it. | MTB-STD-041 2.4 | Tells customers within 72 hours | Service terms, clause 11.2: "The supplier will notify the customer of a security incident within 72 hours of detecting it." | not met | Supplier: 72 hours. Limit: at most 24 hours. 72 is more than 24, so the limit is missed. A missed limit is not met. Check whether the bank can agree a 24-hour notice term. |
| 5 | The supplier has a penetration test carried out at least once a year, and closes critical findings within 30 days. | MTB-STD-041 2.5 | A test every year; critical findings closed within 45 days | Penetration test summary, dated 20 May 2026: "Test carried out annually. Critical findings are closed within 45 days of the report." | not met | Supplier: once a year. Limit: at least once a year. 1 is not less than 1, so the limit is met. Supplier: 45 days. Limit: at most 30 days. 45 is more than 30, so the limit is missed. A missed limit is not met, even though the test itself is yearly. Check the record of how fast critical findings are closed. |
| 6 | Customer information stays in Meridia unless the bank has agreed otherwise in writing. This covers backups. | MTB-STD-041 3.1 | Live archive in Meridia; backups at a second site in Quenmark | Hosting schedule, extract: "Primary site: Meridia. Backup site: Quenmark."; no written agreement from the bank is attached | not met | Backups are held in Quenmark, outside Meridia, and the condition the requirement sets, the bank's agreement in writing, is not shown in the evidence. A condition not shown is not met. Check whether the bank has agreed in writing to backups outside Meridia. |
| 7 | The supplier lists its sub-processors and tells the bank at least 30 days before it adds or changes one. | MTB-STD-041 3.2 | Lists sub-processors; 30 days' notice of a change | Sub-processor list, version 4; service terms, clause 9.1: "The supplier gives the customer 30 days' written notice before it adds or changes a sub-processor." | met | Supplier: 30 days. Limit: at least 30 days. 30 is not less than 30, so the limit is met. The sub-processor list is attached. |
| 8 | At the end of the contract the supplier returns or deletes the bank's information within 60 days and gives a certificate. | MTB-STD-041 3.3 | Deleted within 90 days of the end of the contract | Service terms, clause 20.3: "Customer information is deleted within 90 days of the end of the contract." | not met | Supplier: 90 days. Limit: at most 60 days. 90 is more than 60, so the limit is missed. The evidence does not show a certificate either. Check whether the contract can provide return or deletion within 60 days with a certificate. |
| 9 | The supplier has a business continuity plan that was tested within the last 12 months. | MTB-STD-041 4.1 | Plan last tested on 16 March 2026 | Business continuity test report, extract: "Full test carried out on 16 March 2026. Result: passed." | met | Supplier: test dated 16 March 2026; case date 16 November 2026; age 8 months. Limit: at most 12 months. 8 is not more than 12, so the limit is met. |
| 10 | The recovery time objective for a tier 1 service is no longer than four hours. | MTB-STD-041 4.2 | Recovery time objective of 8 hours | Service schedule, extract: "Recovery time objective: 8 hours." | not met | Supplier: 8 hours. Limit: at most 4 hours. 8 is more than 4, so the limit is missed. A missed limit is not met. |
| 11 | Backups are tested at least twice a year. | MTB-STD-041 4.3 | Test-restored once a year | Backup procedure, extract: "A test restore of backups is carried out once a year." | not met | Supplier: once a year. Limit: at least twice a year. 1 is less than 2, so the limit is missed. A missed frequency is not met. |
| 12 | The contract gives the bank the right to audit the supplier. | MTB-STD-041 5.1 | The contract gives a right to audit | Contract, clause 14.1: "The customer may audit the supplier once a year on 30 days' notice." | met | The answer and the evidence both show what the requirement asks. |
| 13 | An exit plan is agreed before the service starts. | MTB-STD-041 5.2 | To be agreed after signing | Contract, clause 18: "An exit plan is to be agreed after signing." | not met | Planned start of the service: 1 March 2027. No agreed exit plan is attached, and the contract leaves it to be agreed after signing, so the condition that it is agreed before the service starts is not shown. A condition not shown is not met. Check for an exit plan signed by both parties before 1 March 2027. |
| 14 | The contract gives the bank the right to be told of sub-contracting. | MTB-STD-041 5.3 | The contract gives the right to be told | Contract, clause 9.2: "The supplier will tell the customer of any sub-contracting." | met | The answer and the evidence both show what the requirement asks. |
| 15 | A tier 1 supplier holds liability insurance of at least USD 5 million. | MTB-STD-041 5.4 | Liability insurance of USD 2,000,000.00 | Insurance certificate, extract: "Liability limit: USD 2,000,000." | not met | Supplier: USD 2,000,000.00. Limit: at least USD 5,000,000.00. 2,000,000.00 is less than 5,000,000.00, so the limit is missed. A missed limit is not met. |
| 16 | Staff who can reach customer information have passed a background check. | MTB-STD-041 6.1 | Staff who can reach customer information have passed a background check | People procedure, extract: "Every person who can reach customer information passes a background check before they start." | met | The answer and the evidence both show what the requirement asks. |
| 17 | Staff complete security training at least once a year. | MTB-STD-041 6.2 | All staff trained every year | Training record, extract: "Security training completed by all staff on 9 March 2026. The course is run every year." | met | Supplier: once a year, last completed 9 March 2026. Limit: at least once a year. 1 is not less than 1, so the limit is met. |

Recommendation: do not recommend approval: 1. 2.1 (not met): an independent security certification or audit report dated within the last 12 months; 2. 2.3 (partly met): multi-factor authentication for every member of staff who can reach the bank's information, not only administrators, with the policy that shows it; 3. 2.4 (not met): a contract term to tell the bank of a security incident within 24 hours of detecting it; 4. 2.5 (not met): evidence that critical findings are closed within 30 days; 5. 3.1 (not met): backups kept in Meridia, or the bank's agreement in writing to backups outside Meridia; 6. 3.3 (not met): a contract term to return or delete the bank's information within 60 days with a certificate; 7. 4.2 (not met): a recovery time objective of no longer than four hours; 8. 4.3 (not met): backup tests at least twice a year, with the procedure that shows it; 9. 5.2 (not met): an exit plan signed by both parties before the service starts on 1 March 2027; 10. 5.4 (not met): liability insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.00, with the certificate. A tier 1 supplier is approved by the Risk Committee and not by the desk (MTB-STD-041 7.4). A requirement that is not met can be accepted only as a recorded exception approved by the Risk Committee, with an end date (MTB-STD-041 7.5).
